hardware: Apple M4 Max, 48 GiB unified memory, 12 performance + 4 efficiency cores, macOS 26.7
runtime: redlite-generate (native C/Objective-C/Metal, no llama.cpp, no Python), built with -mcpu=native on this machine
prompt: Explain in one sentence why the sky is blue.

runs.label: --cache-mib 4096, expert misses served from SSD (page cache churned by preceding oracle runs)
earlier the same day, 40-token runs, page cache fully warm

long_context.note: token-by-token prefill; llama.cpp argmax identical at positions 1000-1199

regression: scripts/regress_m4.sh: 34/34 on this machine at this commit
caveat: Single machine, single session. Throughput on this 48 GiB machine is bounded by expert miss loading (13-15 ms of the ~30 ms step) when the GGUF is warm in the page cache and drops to ~21 tok/s when misses come from the SSD; the hit rates and SSD bytes per token are prompt-determined and identical to the M4 Pro 24 GiB record. The dev18 figures in benchmarks/m4pro-24gb-native-dev18.json are from the M4 Pro 24 GiB and are not comparable.

resident_ceiling.method: 17408 MiB expert cache (20074 slots), three identical chat turns in one interactive session, temperature 0; third turn has its experts resident

single_300_token_run_17408.note: first-touch misses continue for the whole run; the cache never fills

resident_ceiling.conclusion: With zero misses the current native kernels reach ~43 tok/s (24 ms/step) vs 68 tok/s for llama.cpp fully resident; expert prefetch can recover at most ~20% of decode on this machine. Prompt ingestion (token-by-token, ~25-45 tok/s) is 8-13x behind llama.cpp's batched prefill (339 tok/s): batched prefill is the next milestone (dev20).
